investigation.title: Remote Agent Pods Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-07-08T03:25–03:33Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the 6-node production cluster has only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource, both of which reported insufficient capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the eval runner never received a VM ID or a remote state value, causing all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) to remain absent and the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" (the per-node VM slot quota is exhausted), and the other 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. Preemption was also unavailable on both node groups. The pod remained Unschedulable for 125–148 seconds across all three checks before the eval timed out, producing an empty evidence object and a full contract-gap failure. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agent VM pool in the production-api environment; no evidence of a user-traffic or broader service outage is present in the packet.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-07-08T03:25–03:33Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the 6-node production cluster has only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource, both of which reported insufficient capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" (the per-node VM slot quota is exhausted), and the other 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. Preemption was also unavailable on both node groups. The pod remained Unschedulable for 125–148 seconds across all three checks before the eval timed out, producing an empty evidence object and a full contract-gap failure. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agent VM pool in the production-api environment; no evidence of a user-traffic or broader service outage is present in the packet.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Exhaustion: kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Depleted Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-07-08 with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors reporting zero available nodes: 2 nodes have insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod could never be scheduled, the eval runner never reached the point of creating an agent or collecting any evidence, leaving all 5 required contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) absent.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agents swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource allocation across the 2 nodes that carry that resource type. The remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. With 0/6 nodes schedulable and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod creation attempt times out unscheduled. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure, not an application code defect. No evidence of a user-traffic or production incident signal is present; this is localized to the AURA observability eval for the remote-agents feature in production-api.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: the peer-pod VM slot quota is fully consumed by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new eval pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

SECONDARY — node affinity or node selector misconfiguration: 4 of 6 nodes are excluded by the pod spec's affinity/selector rules, artificially constraining the schedulable pool to only the 2 kata-capable nodes. If the affinity rules are overly restrictive or stale, the effective capacity ceiling is lower than the total cluster size.

TERTIARY — resource leak or runaway workload consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: a prior eval run, a user workload, or a stuck agent pod may be holding VM slots without releasing them, preventing new allocations. The withCleanup wrapper in the runner (source-context run-status-probes.mjs:1916) is designed to release resources, but if a prior run crashed before cleanup, slots may remain held.

QUATERNARY — cluster autoscaler not provisioning additional kata-capable nodes in time: if autoscaling is configured but new kata-capable nodes take longer than the eval timeout (~148s) to become ready, the pod will always time out even if capacity would eventually appear.
